name: Hinge Standouts

card.summary: Hinge Standouts are the most-liked profiles on the dating app's Standouts feed, which looksmaxxing forums catalogue by city and sex as a benchmark of which looks and photos attract the most attention.
card.note: Community-run ratings of real people's photos; informal, not a measured study.

quick.overview:
Hinge is a dating app where users like specific photos or prompts. Its Standouts section surfaces profiles that are popular in an area. On looksmax.org, members post recurring threads listing the Standouts for a city, such as London or New York, split by men and women.

The appearance payoff is as a reference point: users compare what the most-liked profiles look like and how they present themselves, and use that to judge their own photos and looks.
quick.how: A member browses the Standouts section in a given location, lists the profiles seen (usually first names and age range), and others vote or comment on who they think looks best. Some members also post their own test profiles and describe how they perform in the same area.
quick.risks: These are informal ratings of real people on a public forum, and the profiles are strangers' dating photos. Commentary can be harsh and based on appearance, ethnicity or height, and results reflect forum opinions rather than measured data.

lead: Hinge Standouts threads are a recurring genre on looksmax.org. A poster looks at the Standouts section of the Hinge dating app in a particular city, describes it as the most popular profiles in the area, and lists the men or women shown for others to rate. [1][2][3]

Hinge itself was started by Justin McLeod as a desktop service in 2011, became a mobile app in 2012 and launched in February 2013. It is built around liking a specific photo or prompt rather than swiping, and was acquired by Match Group in 2018. [4]

In forum use, Standouts serve as a benchmark: members use the images to discuss which facial features, styling and photo choices appear among the most-liked profiles, and compare their own profiles against them. [1][3]

chain: Adjust one's own photos and looks accordingly
angle.text: Members treat Standouts as a visible sample of what currently attracts likes in a city. It is used to calibrate photos, grooming and style rather than to change one's features directly.

infobox: City-by-city threads for women and men

paras: The threads follow a template: a title with the city, sex and date, a statement of the age range sampled (for example women aged 20-30 with no ethnicities filtered out), a list of first names with screenshots, and an invitation to vote on who is best-looking. [1][3]

Examples from July 2024 cover London women, London men and New York women. One poster says they were running a test profile in London at the time and describes Standouts as the most popular profiles in the area. [1][2][3]

Members use the lists to discuss who ranks highest and why, including height, facial features and ethnic background. Other threads cover Standouts by region, such as northern England and Scotland, and separate lists labelled 'slayers'. [5][7]
Some posters compare their own test profile's performance to the Standouts as a rough measure of how their looks do on the app. [3]
No studies found. Hinge describes its recommended 'most compatible' feature, based on a matching algorithm, but no published study examines the Standouts section or the forum threads. [4]

timeline.event: Justin McLeod starts the desktop service that becomes Hinge. [4]
Hinge mobile app launches in February. [4]
Match Group acquires a majority of Hinge. [4]

lore.intro: Standouts threads are used on looksmax.org as informal polls of who looks best among popular dating profiles. [1][3]

claims.claim: Standouts show what gets the most matches in a city
claims.believers: Posters describe Standouts as the most popular profiles in the area and use them as a standard. [1][2]
claims.experts: No published study has examined the Hinge Standouts feature.
